record.name: Compatible supply and converging bottlenecks
record.role: Converts independently manufactured inputs into a common finished-system basis.
record.description: Accelerator packages require compatible logic dies, memory stacks, substrates and integration capacity to arrive together. HBM is manufactured and assembled on its own path before package integration. Facility deployment adds boards, racks, electrical service, cooling and software readiness. Counts from these stages use different units and cannot simply be added. A bill of materials converts each usable input into a possible number of finished units. The smallest compatible supply then bounds output for the chosen interval. TSMC’s packaging descriptions illustrate the convergence, while the laboratory model must keep screening, assembly yield and qualification as distinct steps.

interfaces.name: Compatible screened inputs
interfaces.signal: Logic, HBM stacks, substrates and assembly slots

interfaces.name: Finished system output
interfaces.signal: Packages or racks surviving the explicitly modeled stages

record.tradeoff: Building inventory of one input may reduce later delay but ties up capital and does not compensate for a missing compatible component.
record.whyAI: Logic-wafer expansion cannot independently establish AI deployment capacity when memory, packaging or powered-rack readiness binds.
record.scale: Manufacturing supply to commissioned hall; time-dependent model
mechanism: Select a concrete bill of materials and finished-system boundary.
Convert each available qualified input into equivalent finished units.
Identify compatibility restrictions rather than pooling unrelated generations or package types.
Apply only the remaining assembly/test losses to already-screened input quantities.
Compare the resulting output with downstream rack and facility readiness during the same period.
record.misconception: HBM does not appear after package manufacture; its own manufacturing branch converges with logic and package materials.

check.question: If each package needs four HBM stacks, what can 400 compatible good stacks support before later losses?
check.explanation: The bill of materials converts stack count into a compatible finished-package bound.

science.title: Converging supply bound
science.explanation: Si is usable input-i units and bi input-i units per finished product; Ncomplete counts finished products.
science.assumptions: Inputs are compatible and coavailable; later yield, timing and set overlap require additional treatment.

record.learningObjective: Convert supply quantities to one finished-unit basis without yield double counting.
record.engineeringExample: Synthetic package needs one logic die, four HBM stacks and one substrate. Supplies of 150, 400 and 120 good units respectively bound assembly starts at 100, before any new assembly losses.
record.evidenceNotes: No vendor capacity, queue or HBM wafer-intensity number is invented. Synthetic inputs are explicitly screened, avoiding repeated raw-die yield penalties.
record.scope: Trace compatible component rates, a bounded qualification/ramp scenario and package backlog; this is not a detailed fab queue or operator-allocation simulator.
